benefits: The KTH Scholarship covers the tuition fee at KTH for the first year of the master's programme.

official.application_route: Apply for a KTH master's programme at universityadmissions.se as first priority and pay the SEK 900 application fee, then submit the scholarship form on the KTH Scholarship page between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to fee-paying students; citizens of an EU/EEA country or Switzerland are generally not required to pay application and tuition fees, while non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are usually required to pay them.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the KTH scholarships are open to all fee-paying applicants, with no country restriction stated on the scholarship page.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All master's programmes with two years spent at KTH, the joint master's programmes in Molecular Techniques in Life Science and Biostatistics and Data Science, and the one-year Architectural Lighting Design; joint Erasmus+ and EIT programmes and Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering are excluded.
official.duration: One or two-year master's programme; the scholarship covers the tuition fee for the first and the second year provided the first-year study results are satisfactory.
official.description: The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee of a one or two year master's programme at KTH Royal Institute of Technology for fee-paying students; it does not include living costs. The selection process focuses on academic excellence and the drive to contribute to sustainable development. In 2026, 9% of scholarship applicants admitted to a programme were nominated for the scholarship (65 out of 718).
official.program_type: Tuition fee scholarship for fee-paying master's programme applicants
official.english_requirement: English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2, for example an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 4.5; depending on the country of previous studies the requirement can also be met through completed upper secondary or university studies (admission requirement of the master's programme).

applicant_utility.summary: The KTH Scholarship erases the full tuition fee - SEK 385,000 for most two-year programmes - but you must first apply for the KTH master's programme at universityadmissions.se, rank it first and pay the SEK 900 application fee; only then can you submit the scholarship form between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027. There is no scholarship essay or extra upload: KTH judges you on the transcripts, CV and documents already filed with universityadmissions.se by the document deadline, plus how you argue you will contribute to the sustainable development goals. With only about 9% of admitted fee-paying applicants nominated (65 of 718 in 2026), treat it as a reach award and fund Stockholm living costs separately.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-paying non-EU/EEA applicants with strong grades from a well-ranked bachelor's university, a credible sustainable-development motivation, and a two-year KTH programme ranked first at universityadmissions.se.
application_readiness_checklist: Complete the universityadmissions.se application by 15 January 2027 with the KTH programme ranked first, and pay the SEK 900 application fee - KTH warns that assessment depends on payment.

Assemble the degree certificate, transcripts with the grading scale, CV and passport early so everything reaches University Admissions by the document deadline (2 February per the scholarship page; 1 February per programme pages); there is no later fix window.
Draft your sustainable-development motivation against the specific SDGs listed on your chosen programme's page before the scholarship form opens on 1 December 2026.

Confirm the programme is eligible: two years spent at KTH, Molecular Techniques in Life Science, Biostatistics and Data Science, or the one-year Architectural Lighting Design - not an Erasmus+/EIT/COSSE programme.
Plan proof of funds for Stockholm living costs (KTH's 2026 student budget examples total SEK 7,850-13,000 per month) for the residence permit, since the scholarship covers none of it.
Note that second-year tuition renewal depends on satisfactory first-year results - build that academic performance plan into year one from the start.
common_rejection_risks: Listing KTH below first priority - scholarships cannot be awarded for second, third or fourth priority programmes, no matter how strong the file.
Missing the document deadline, which leaves the universityadmissions.se file incomplete and starves the scholarship evaluation of its only evidence base.
A generic or thin sustainable-development motivation - KTH explicitly scores this criterion, and it is where otherwise similar GPA profiles are separated.
Applying with a joint Erasmus+/EIT or Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering programme as first priority, which are excluded from this scholarship.
Weak first-year study results, which end the tuition coverage after year one even for recipients.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Stockholm are fully on you: KTH's 2026 student budget examples total SEK 7,850-13,000 per month (housing, food, transport, hobbies), plus one-off settling-in costs such as housing deposits, and the SEK 900 application fee is never refunded.
document_audit: There are no scholarship-specific documents - anything weak or missing in your universityadmissions.se file directly weakens the scholarship case.
Transcripts must show the grading scale actually used; unexplained scales stall assessment at University Admissions and feed straight into the scholarship review.
Final-year applicants must follow University Admissions' document instructions for unfinished degrees rather than waiting for a graduation certificate that arrives after the deadline.
English test evidence (IELTS 6.5 or equivalent) must already be valid at application time - the programme admission, and therefore scholarship eligibility, cannot rest on a promised later test.
alerts: The scholarship window (1 December 2026 - 15 January 2027) is much narrower than the programme application window (16 October 2026 - 15 January 2027) - diary both openings and closes.
Scholarship results land on 1 April 2027, which is tight against residence-permit and housing timing for an August 2027 start, so keep backup funding plans warm.

The award rate is roughly one nominated scholarship for every eleven admitted fee-paying applicants (65 of 718 in 2026), so apply in parallel for Swedish Institute or other funding rather than relying on this one.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply and upload documents at universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 (documents by the early-February deadline), then complete the online scholarship form on the KTH Scholarship page between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027; KTH reuses the admissions file for the scholarship decision and publishes results on 1 April 2027.
